Article Title: ‘Bigger than Emergency’: Band-aid over mouth, Mamata Banerjee detained in Delhi protest
Article Text:
Mamata Banerjee wears band-aid over mouth before Delhi detention

NEW DELHI: Former West Bengal chief minister and Trinamool Congress (TMC) chief Mamata Banerjee pasted a band-aid over her mouth as a mark of protest before being detained from South Avenue in Delhi along with party leaders Derek O'Brien, Dola Sen and other members.CPM leaders were also detained during the demonstration, PTI reported.Banerjee, who staged a dharna at a bus stand in Delhi’s South Avenue, said the situation appeared to be “bigger than Emergency”.Delhi Police continued to detain protesters, citing the lack of permission for the demonstration. Security was tightened at multiple locations across the national capital as CJP activists remained firm on their call to protest against the Election Commission over alleged voter disenfranchisement. Entry points to Delhi were placed under heightened security, while 46 Metro stations remained closed.Earlier, CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke and his associates were detained at Delhi airport as they deboarded their flight from Mumbai, where Dipke had been travelling to participate in the protest.Content creator Dhruv Rathee was also detained from his Gurugram residence.In a pre-recorded video made on Friday in anticipation of a possible arrest, Dipke said the party’s national organisation in-charge, Ajinkya Shinde, would lead the protest at Jantar Mantar until he, spokesperson Saurav Das and co-convener Ashutosh Ranka were released from detention.Meanwhile, security has been stepped up at multiple locations across Delhi as CJP activists remain determined to go ahead with their protest against the Election Commission. Entry points to the national capital are under heightened surveillance, while 46 Metro stations remain closed.
Article Summary: Former West Bengal chief minister and Trinamool Congress (TMC) chief Mamata Banerjee pasted a band-aid over her mouth as a mark of protest. She was detained from South Avenue in Delhi along with party leaders Derek O'Brien, Dola Sen and other members. CPM leaders were also detained during the demonstration, PTI reported.

Article Title: SIR protest: Former CMs Mamata Banerjee, Pinarayi Vijayan and Arvind Kejriwal among opposition leaders detained from Delhi
Article Text:
Pinarayi Vijayan, Mamata Banerjee

CPM leaders condemn police action

NEW DELHI: Former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee and Kerala leader of opposition Pinarayi Vijayan were detained by Delhi Police on Saturday during protests against Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.Banerjee was detained from South Avenue along with Trinamool Congress leaders Derek O'Brien, Dola Sen and other party members, PTI reported. CPM leaders were also detained during the demonstration.Meanwhile, former Delhi chief minister Arvind Kejriwal was also detained.Following their detention, CPM leaders took to social media to condemn the police action, while party leaders in Kerala denounced the move and called for protests.In a Facebook post shared after being taken into custody, Vijayan accused the NDA government of turning the national capital into an "open prison" and attempting to suppress protests through the deployment of armed police and paramilitary forces.Vijayan alleged that the protest was against attempts, with the support of those in power, to undermine people's voting rights, which he described as the foundation of democracy.He accused the Centre of attempting to turn India into a "police state" by detaining protesters on their way to demonstrations and arresting people indiscriminately. He said the struggle to protect the Constitution and voting rights would continue.CPM leader P Rajeev also recorded a video from the police vehicle in which he was being taken after his detention, saying the protest to save democracy in India would continue despite the arrests."All central leaders of CPM took part in the protest. They have arrested and shifted us in a jail-like vehicle. We are travelling in a vehicle for the past one hour," he said.Rajeev described the agitation as a landmark protest in the country's history and urged those who believed in democracy to carry it forward more forcefully.Meanwhile, CPM leader P A Muhammad Riyas condemned the police action in a Facebook post, describing it as "undemocratic".Riyas, the Beypore MLA and Vijayan's son-in-law, said authorities should not assume that they could suppress protests by arresting party leaders. He maintained that the right to protest was fundamental to democracy and said the party would intensify its struggle to protect democratic rights.Senior CPM leader V Sivankutty shared a social media post carrying the slogan "Hum Leke Rahenge", while the party's Kerala unit called for protests against the police action in Delhi.
Article Summary: Former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee and Kerala leader of opposition Pinarayi Vijayan were detained by Delhi Police. CPM leaders took to social media to condemn the police action, while party leaders in Kerala denounced the move and called for protests.

Article Title: 'Anarchists have failed, planned to hold Delhi hostage': BJP slams Jantar Mantar stir

NEW DELHI: BJP MP Sambit Patra on Saturday termed the Cockroach Janata Party's (CJP) proposed protest at Delhi's Jantar Mantar a "flop show". The BJP MP claimed that the "anarchists" who wanted to hold Delhi "hostage" have failed."Jantar Mantar's story is not India's story. What is happening at Jantar Mantar, what you can see on TV and a few social media handles, is not India's story. India is calm and going ahead under good governance. We have been seeing that a few anarchist forces have been spreading anarchy in a corner of Delhi for the past few days. But today the anarchists have failed. The flop show of anarchist elements has completely collapsed. There was an attempt to hold India, the national capital, captive; that there be arson here, that there be violence here. But today, 'loktantra' has triumphed over bheedtantra," the BJP MP said.He alleged that the protesters had attempted to hold the country and the national capital hostage and were seeking to create violence."They were trying to hold India hostage, make the national capital hostage. They wanted violence," he said.The remarks came amid a political row over the CJP's proposed demonstration against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. The outfit had called the protest over allegations of voter-list manipulation during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and changes relating to Form 6, which is used for voter registration.Earlier on Saturday, the CJP claimed that its leaders Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were detained by Delhi Police from inside an aircraft after it landed in the national capital. The leaders had travelled from Mumbai to attend the planned demonstration.In a video shared by the outfit, Dipke accused the police of preventing them from disembarking and described the alleged action as dictatorship. Police personnel reportedly told the leaders that they did not have permission to hold the protest at Jantar Mantar.Police sources told news agency PTI that the three leaders were taken to different locations, with Dipke taken to Gurugram, Ranka to Dwarka in Delhi and Das to another location in the city.The developments came as BJP president Nitin Nabin separately accused Congress leader Rahul Gandhi, AAP convenor Arvind Kejriwal and the CJP of attempting to create anarchy and destabilise the country. He alleged that their actions were driven by political ambitions and claimed that they were acting in collusion with foreign forces, charges that the opposition leaders have not been shown responding to in the statements provided.

Article Title: FIR against Rahul, Priyanka Gandhi over 'assault' during anti-Gyanesh Kumar protest in Delhi

NEW DELHI: Delhi Police has registered an FIR against Congress leaders Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra for allegedly assaulting police personnel and obstructing government work during a protest in the capital, news agency PTI reported, citing police sources on Thursday.The FIR invokes various sections related to allegedly assaulting and manhandling police personnel, obstructing public servants in the discharge of their duties and misbehaviour with police officers.The action comes a day after INDIA bloc MPs were stopped by Delhi Police while attempting to march towards Jantar Mantar for a protest against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.Several other Congress leaders and party workers who took part in the demonstration have also been named in the FIR, police sources said.Police are examining the allegations and the role of those involved in the protest.Earlier on Wednesday, Rahul, Priyanka had led INDIA bloc leaders in a street protest, demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.Police detained 91 people during the demonstration, including several MPs and other political leaders.The protest took an intense turn after police stopped the protesters while they were travelling in buses towards Jantar Mantar for a surprise sit-in.The leaders had earlier attended a lunch meeting at a South Indian vegetarian restaurant on Janpath.Priyanka and several other women leaders lay on the road holding copies of the Constitution. They were later removed and taken away in police buses as opposition members raised slogans.MPs from the Congress, Trinamool Congress, CPM, CPI, RJD, IUML and several other parties were among those participating in the protest.
Article Summary: Rahul, Priyanka led INDIA bloc leaders in a street protest, demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Police detained 91 people during the demonstration, including several MPs and other political leaders. Police are examining the allegations and the role of those involved in the protest.

NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke was taken to Gurugram after being detained by Delhi Police at the Indira Gandhi International Airport on Saturday, ahead of the outfit’s proposed protest against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.CJP leaders Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das were also detained. Traffic diversions would be implemented depending on the prevailing law and order situation.According to the traffic advisory, affected stretches include the Ashoka Road-Jantar Mantar Road roundabout, Tolstoy Marg-Janpath crossing, Jai Singh Road-Sansad Marg crossing, Rail Bhawan roundabout, Patel Chowk, Gol Dak Khana and Windsor Place.Delhi Police denied permission for the proposed demonstration, citing law and order concerns and the possibility of inconvenience to residents. Article Title: 'Surrounded by 35 cops': CJP flags 'illegal' detention of Ratna Singh ahead of Jantar Mantar protest
Article Text: NEW DELHI: The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) on Saturday termed the detention of its founder and leaders “illegal”, alleging that the outfit’s head of legal affairs, Ratna Singh, was also being held inside a car by police.In the run-up to the proposed showdown at Jantar Mantar against chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke and leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were detained shortly after arriving at Delhi airport from Mumbai.The party’s official handle said Ratna Singh was being detained inside a car, alleging that she was “surrounded by 35 cops and the DCP, who are refusing to let her out”.The detentions unfolded on Saturday, hours before the CJP’s planned protest at Jantar Mantar. Opposition parties, including the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) and Left parties, had also expressed support for the demonstration and said they would join the protest.The CJP had called for the demonstration in the wake of the Election Commission’s large-scale special intensive revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. The outfit is demanding the removal of chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.

Welcome to the New Delhi, modelled on the New Jammu and Kashmir," Abdullah said in a post on X.He was referring to reports of internet service suspensions in parts of Central Delhi ahead of a planned protest against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar on Saturday.Security arrangements have been tightened across New Delhi ahead of the ‘Jantar Mantar 2.0’ protest scheduled for Saturday, with more than 35,000 Delhi Police and paramilitary personnel deployed. The demonstration, called by CJP to seek accountability over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, is set to take place at Jantar Mantar despite police denying permission.The Union Home Secretary has also directed states and Union Territories to maintain law and order.Roads leading to Jantar Mantar are set to be closed, while police have barricaded stretches including Ashoka Road, Tolstoy Marg and Jantar Mantar Lane, where violence, stone-pelting or clashes were reported during the previous protest on July 20.Mobile internet services are to be suspended within a 4-km radius of Jantar Mantar.Following a request from Delhi Police, the Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC) initially announced the closure of entry and exit gates at 57 stations from 9 pm on October 9, along with reduced train frequency. The list was later curtailed to 45 stations, after the Supreme Court directed the Centre to reconsider the sweeping restrictions. The curbs are expected to remain in place until 6 pm on October 10.

Article Title: Judge recuses from Punjab government appeal case
Article Text:
SC: Thousand sources... don’t now where attacks will come

NEW DELHI: Justice Sheel Nagu, who was chief justice of Punjab and Haryana HC for nearly two years prior to his elevation to Supreme Court , on Friday recused from hearing Punjab govt's appeal against the HC's order directing a CBI probe into an alleged bribe syndicate, having links with the CM's OSD, that influenced postings, transfers and tenders.At the commencement of hearing, Justice Dipankar Datta said Justice Nagu wants to recuse from the case, even though senior advocate Jaideep Gupta, appearing for Punjab govt, said the state did not have any objection to him remaining a part of the bench.Hinting that Justice Nagu’s continuation on the bench might be turned into a controversy, Justice Datta said, “These days there are a thousand sources. We do not know where the attacks will come.” In the recent past, AAP supremo Arvind Kejriwal had raised questions about a Delhi HC judge’s impartiality and sought her recusal from hearing an appeal related to a criminal case against him.When Gupta reiterated his request, Justice Datta said SC has 17 benches and the case could go to another. The order stated: “Re-list this petition before a bench of which JusticeNagu is not a member.”
Article Summary: Justice Sheel Nagu was chief justice of Punjab and Haryana HC for nearly two years prior to his elevation to Supreme Court. Punjab govt's appeal against HC's order directing a CBI probe into an alleged bribe syndicate that influenced postings, transfers and tenders.

Article Title: Assembly bypolls: TVK wins 2 seats in TN, BJP also bags 2 in Bengal
Article Text:
A victory for political decorum and personal decency, says Vijay

CHENNAI/KOLKATA/PUDUCHERRY/GUWAHATI: TVK cleared its first test barely five months after forming govt in Tamil Nadu, winning the bypolls in two assembly constituencies, while in West Bengal, BJP retained Nandigram - CM Suvendu Adhikari's backyard - and wrested Rejinagar from AJUP (Aam Janata Unnayan Party), winning both assembly bypolls in its first electoral test since coming to office in state.All-India NR Congress, an NDA ally, retained Thattanchavady assembly segment, with Ashok Anand defeating his nearest Congress rival by over 8,400 votes. BJP regained Assam's Nagaon Lok Sabha constituency, with ex-IAS officer Devasish Sharma securing about 50% of the vote. AIUDF chief Badruddin Ajmal finished second, followed by Congress's Sibamoni Bora. Sharma, who was Nagaon district commissioner when he took VRS and had joined BJP last month, led Ajmal by over 1.5 lakh votes, while Bora trailed by over 1.2 lakh votes.Though Madurantakam and Dharapuram in Tamil Nadu presented different political terrain, TVK won both seats with comfortable margins by fielding former AIADMK MLAs Maragatham Kumaravel and P Sathyabama, who had joined the governing party barely 20 days after the assembly election results in May. Sathyabama won Dharapuram by 9,471 votes, while Maragatham secured Madurantakam with a margin of 20,040 votes.DMK finished second in both seats, while AIADMK, which had won the two segments in the April assembly election, was pushed to third. The results increase TVK’s strength in the 234-member assembly from 107 to 109. “This is a victory for political decorum and personal decency. The victory is a verdict against derogatory remarks targeting women, personal attacks and betrayal. This winning streak will continue,” chief minister C Joseph Vijay posted on X.DMK president MK Stalin called it a “temporary victory for betrayal”.BJP’s two victories in Bengal take its strength to 209 in an assembly where it faces a fractured opposition, a part of which has been toeing the govt line on key issues. The saffron party retained Nandigram, where a bypoll was necessitated by Adhikari’s decision to vacate the seat in favour of Bhabanipur, by a record 1,22,753 votes.Adhikari had won Nandigram in the April assembly polls by 9,665 votes. Sanchita Dey Pradhan, fielded by Mamata Trinamool Congress, had withdrawn from the race on Sept 17 after meeting Adhikari in Kolkata. Congress candidate Milan Pradhan, who finished second with the backing of Mamata Trinamool Congress, spent 11 days in police custody over FIRs lodged 19 years ago. He was able to campaign for only four days after Calcutta HC granted him interim bail on Sept 29.The comfortable wins in the Muslim-dominated seats of Nandigram and Rejinagar signal a potential shift in Bengal’s political arithmetic. In Rejinagar, BJP candidate Shankharavh Sarkar won by 75,816 votes, pushing AJUP, which won the seat in the April poll, to second place. Muslims constitute 72% of the electorate in Rejinagar, in Murshidabad.
Article Summary: TVK cleared first test barely five months after forming govt in Tamil Nadu. In West Bengal, BJP retained Nandigram and wrested Rejinagar from AJUP. In Assam, BJP regained Assam's Nagaon Lok Sabha constituency.

Article Title: No correlation between SIR deletions & assembly poll results: Bengal CEO
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: The chief electoral officer of West Bengal Friday dismissed as "misleading and speculative" claims made in an "analysis" posted on YouTube that deletions made during special intensive revision in the state had a direct bearing on the outcome of the recent assembly elections.In a post on X, the CEO quoted the analysis by DeKoder and countered it with electoral data from five West Bengal seats that saw the highest SIR deletions - four of them were won by Trinamool Congress and one went to BJP. As for the five constituencies with the lowest SIR deletions, BJP ended up winning in all.Refuting the claims made in the YouTube video - which relied on electoral data from 25 seats with the highest and lowest SIR deletions, and pointed to -10.5% and -5.3% swings respectively, for TMC - West Bengal's top electoral officer said "the electoral data... does not support the political narrative".The officer also dismissed the claim that women accounted for 62% of the electors deleted through SIR in West Bengal. "The claim... is unverified. As per the total data on deletion of invalid entries (excluding adjudication), around 50% or half of the deletions related to women," he posted on X.Regarding the DeKoder claim that deletions of Muslim electors were 52% more than those of non-Muslim electors, the CEO pointed out there was no data based on religious identity of the voters."Hence the analysis claimed is based on mere unverified assumptions," he posted."...The facts do not support the allegations," the officer stated and asserted that no voter could be deleted without due process. "Issuance of notice, an opportunity for hearing and a speaking order by the ERO (electoral registration officer) are part of the safeguards. Appeals are available at two levels," he added.The CEO said SIR was not about deleting genuine voters but about protecting the integrity of the electoral roll and was being conducted in accordance with Article 324 of Constitution and Section 21 of R P Act 1950, with due process and safeguards. "SIR is a lawful, transparent and ongoing exercise to ensure that every eligible elector is on the roll and that ineligible entries are removed. Electoral rolls must be based on facts - not speculation," he noted.
Article Summary: The chief electoral officer of West Bengal Friday dismissed as "misleading and speculative" claims made in an "analysis" posted on YouTube. The CEO quoted the analysis by DeKoder and countered it with electoral data from five West Bengal seats that saw highest SIR deletions.

Article Title: Amid Form 7 bulk filing row, Election Commission limits it to 10 per elector
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Election Commission Friday, to discourage bulk submissions of Form 7 (objection to inclusion of an elector in the electoral roll), capped the maximum number of these applications that may be filed by an individual elector during the claims and objections period of special and summary revisions to 10.For Form 7 applications filed by an individual elector during the period of continuous update of the electoral roll, the upper limit shall be five per month.The ceilings - which follow Congress flagging bulk filings across many constituencies in Karnataka, including Ballari where a single BJP worker allegedly submitted 7,561 Form 7 applications - will apply to filings by individual electors both in online and offline modes.In a letter to chief electoral officers of states and UTs, EC explained that while the number of applications to be filed online by an individual elector had been fixed as six at a time, subject to disposal, the number of physical forms presented in bulk had not been defined and was left to the judgement of electoral registration officers (ERO). The new limits seek to remove any scope for ambiguity, an EC officer told TOI.According to Rule 13(2) of Registration of Electors Rules (RER) 1960, every objection to the proposed inclusion of name or application for deletion of name in the electoral roll of a constituency is to be referred only by a person whose name figures in the roll of that constituency.For the SIR period, EC has allowed booth-level agents of political parties to submit to a booth level officer Form 7 applications in bulk, with a limit of 50 forms per day before the draft publication and 10 forms per day thereafter.The poll panel Friday said any claim or objection not lodged within the specified period or in the form and manner specified in the rules, shall be rejected by ERO, who will also verify the applicant's name in the electors' list.Once a Form 7 application is found in line with norms, the ERO shall first issue a notice to the objector, hear him personally, record his statem-ents separately for each Form 7 and satisfy himself about the validity of the objections.EC directed EROs to take action against false and fabricated Form 7s, including prosecution of the applicant under R P Act 1950 for knowingly making a false statement or declaration in writing.
Article Summary: Election Commission Friday capped the maximum number of these applications that may be filed by an individual elector during the claims and objections period of special and summary revisions to 10. The ceilings follow Congress flagging bulk filings across many constituencies in Karnataka, including Ballari.

Article Title: ‘I will live in Dubai with a 10-year golden visa’: Humayun Kabir after son loses bypoll
Article Text:
His remarks came hours after BJP candidate Shankharavh Sarkar defeated Kabir’s son, Golam Nabi Azad, the AJUP nominee, by a margin of 75,816 votes in Rejinagar

NEW DELHI: Aam Janata Unnayan Party (AJUP) chief Humayun Kabir on Friday said he would move to Dubai on a 10-year golden visa after completing the mosque he has promised to build in West Bengal’s Murshidabad district, following his son’s crushing defeat in the Rejinagar bypoll.Kabir, the MLA from Nowda, said the mosque, modelled on the Babri Masjid, would be completed by December 6, 2028. Its foundation stone was laid in Rejinagar on December 6, 2025."I will live in Dubai with a 10-year golden visa," he said, as quoted by news agency PTI.His remarks came hours after BJP candidate Shankharavh Sarkar defeated Kabir’s son, Golam Nabi Azad, the AJUP nominee, by a margin of 75,816 votes in Rejinagar, a Muslim-majority constituency in Murshidabad district.The result marks a dramatic reversal for Kabir’s party. Azad had won the seat by nearly 59,000 votes in the West Bengal Assembly elections held barely five months ago, defeating his nearest BJP rival.Reacting to the bypoll outcome, Kabir alleged that the BJP’s victory was secured through the use of the police administration rather than public support. He accused Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari, who also holds the home portfolio, and Murshidabad district police officers of working to ensure the BJP candidate’s victory over the past two months."This is not a people's mandate; the police administration was used to ensure the victory of the BJP in the seat," he asserted.The BJP’s victory in Rejinagar has drawn attention because of the constituency’s substantial Muslim electorate, which has traditionally played a significant role in the Trinamool Congress’s electoral fortunes in the state.Adhikari, however, claimed that the result reflected growing support for the BJP among minority voters. He said Muslims had responded to his appeal for political cooperation and rejected what he described as misleading narratives about the party.The chief minister also took a swipe at Kabir, arguing that his attacks on the BJP had alienated voters.The BJP’s breakthrough in Rejinagar came alongside a decisive victory in Nandigram, where its candidate Hasirani Rath defeated Congress nominee Milan Pradhan by 1,22,753 votes.The twin victories have provided the BJP with an opportunity to project its growing political reach in West Bengal, while the Rejinagar result poses a setback for Kabir’s AJUP.
Article Summary: Aam Janata Unnayan Party (AJUP) chief Humayun Kabir said he would move to Dubai on a 10-year golden visa after completing the mosque he has promised to build. His remarks came hours after BJP candidate Shankharavh Sarkar defeated Kabir’s son, Golam Nabi Azad, by a margin of 75,816 votes in Rejinagar.

NEW DELHI: INDIA bloc leaders on Friday met President Droupadi Murmu and submitted a memorandum outlining four demands, as the opposition intensified its campaign against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.In the memorandum submitted to the President, the opposition demanded: CEC’s resignation, scrapping of assembly elections held over the last two years, suspension of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and a return to paper ballots.“We urge you to take cognisance of this grave situation and use your good offices to ensure that the following demands are addressed without delay,” the memorandum read, listing four demands, including the restoration of 13.30 crore voters allegedly deleted from electoral rolls.The memorandum added: “We approach you because, in moments when every other door has been closed, the people of India look to the Office of the President as the final guardian of that covenant...”After meeting Murmu, Congress leader Rahul Gandhi said he had expected the President to deny that vote theft was taking place but was surprised by her response.“I expected President to deny that 'vote chori' is taking place; I was shocked, stunned that she accepted what we said,” Rahul said.He also announced that opposition leaders would approach the Supreme Court on Monday. “We will go to Supreme Court on Monday to meet Chief Justice of India and hand over memorandum to him,” he said.The delegation included Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge, Former West Bengal CM Mamata Banerjee, Jammu and Kashmir chief minister Omar Abdullah and leaders from other INDIA bloc parties.Earlier, Opposition MPs marched from Parliament House towards Vijay Chowk carrying a “Save Democracy” banner but were stopped by police barricades.The latest action follows several days of protests against Gyanesh Kumar.

Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijit Dipke, along with Chief Spokesperson Saurav Das, National Spokesperson Ashutosh Ranka and Singer Vishal Dadlani during a protest seeking Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation over voter roll deletions at Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Park.

Journalist Roshie detained: Neha

NEW DELHI: The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke in another X post on Monday claimed that the local Deputy Commissioner of Police (DCP) in his hometown had “suddenly gone on leave” and that a new officer had been brought in to take charge.Dipke’s remarks came amid party's earlier claim that he and fellow CJP leaders Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Dass could be arrested before October 10 under the National Security Act (NSA) or other provisions.AISA national president Neha Bora on Monday claimed that protesting journalists have been detained at the Delhi Cantonment Police Station.In a post on X, Neha said "Rosy and other protesting journalists are detained at Delhi Cantt PS. Team of lawyer comrades are in touch with them.But if any lawyer can be at the PS immediately, pls DM."Rosie is among the three female journalists who filed complaint alleging sexual harassment by police personnel during a protest in the New Delhi area on October 3.The complants have been transferred to the Crime Branch at Kamla Market for further action.Delhi Police also detained several protesters outside Parliament Street Police Station who were demonstrating over an alleged incident of sexual misconduct involving three women journalists during an October 3 protest at Jantar Mantar.The protesters alleged that they had been demonstrating since 6pm on Sunday, demanding registration of an FIR in the case. Police detained them around 7am on Monday following a clash, with protesters alleging they were treated poorly despite only seeking registration of an FIR. Trinamool Congress (TMC) MP Derek O’Brien also extended support to Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leaders as party spokesperson Ashutosh Ranka claimed that multiple sources had warned that the three could be arrested before October 10 under the National Security Act (NSA) or other equivalent provisions.“With you all the way 🪳🪳stay strong. ‘10 Oct poora desh aa raha hai…’,” O’Brien said in a post on X while replying to Dipke.CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke reacting to the claim said they would not be intimidated by the possibility of action under laws such as the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA) or National Security Act (NSA).“If the Govt believes that the threat of UAPA, NSA or years behind bars will scare us into silence, it won’t,” Dipke said in a post on X, adding that the protesters were prepared to spend “months or years in jail” but would not back down from their campaign to “save democracy”.He further said that they follow the path shown by Mahatma Gandhi and continue to resist “peacefully and non-violently”, despite what he described as attempts by the state to intimidate them.The developments come amid the CJP-led campaign against the Election Commission’s Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Article Title: ‘300+ calls and counting’: CJP’s Saurav Das alleges Delhi Police leaked his number ahead of Jantar Mantar stir
Article Text:
Saurav Das, a spokesperson for Cockroach Janta Party, reported that his phone number has been leaked





NEW DELHI: 'I have been bombarded with relentless phone calls (300+ and counting)', Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) spokesperson Saurav Das on Saturday alleged that Delhi Police had leaked his phone number while circulating documents related to the party’s previous protest and its latest letter denying permission for a proposed protest at Jantar Mantar. He said he had received more than 300 calls and numerous WhatsApp messages within an hour.In a post on X, Das said, "As part of what appears to be a coordinated campaign, my phone number has been leaked, and I have been bombarded with relentless phone calls (300+ and counting) and WhatsApp messages over the past hour alone"."The number was leaked by the Delhi Police while circulating the undertaking form from our previous protest and its latest letter rejecting permission," Saurav said.Criticising media organisations for circulating the documents without concealing his number, Das said, "Special thanks to the ever-compliant media organisations, specifically an infamous agency I’m told, that couldn’t be bothered to redact my number before breathlessly circulating these documents on social media, as though they laid their hands on the Pentagon Papers!"Meanwhile, Delhi Police has tightened security across the national capital ahead of the CJP’s proposed protest at Jantar Mantar on Saturday against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged voter-list manipulation during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.Earlier, police denied permission for the demonstration, citing insufficient notice and alleged violations of directions issued during an earlier protest. Joint Commissioner of Police Nupur Prasad said the application was submitted on October 7, just three days before the proposed gathering, whereas the prescribed notice period is at least 10 days.Around 25,000 police and paramilitary personnel have been deployed across Delhi, while entry and exit restrictions have been imposed at 45 metro stations. Security has also been tightened at the capital’s borders, railway stations, bus terminals and other sensitive locations.
Article Summary: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) spokesperson Saurav Das alleged that Delhi Police had leaked his phone number. He said he had received more than 300 calls and numerous WhatsApp messages within an hour. Delhi Police has tightened security across the national capital ahead of the CJP’s proposed protest at Jantar Mantar on Saturday.

Article Title: Tamil Nadu CM Vijay hosts Rahul Gandhi at Neelankarai, reinforces alliance bonhomie
Article Text:
Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay is hosting Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi and senior Congress leaders for lunch





CHENNAI: Chief minister C Joseph Vijay is hosting Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi and senior Congress leaders for lunch at his Neelankarai residence on Saturday, in a show of bonhomie between the alliance partners. The meeting comes a day after the TVK-led front won its first electoral test, retaining the Madurantakam and Dharapuram assembly constituencies in the October 6 bypolls.TNCC president Manickam Tagore and other party functionaries accorded a warm reception to Rahul Gandhi at Chennai airport. He then proceeded to Vijay’s residence for the lunch meeting, which is expected to strengthen ties between the two parties.The meeting also comes against the backdrop of protests demanding the removal of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, which Rahul Gandhi has supported, and the TVK government’s action against students protesting in Chennai over the same issue. The contrasting positions could bring the issue into focus during Rahul Gandhi’s visit, even as the two parties seek to strengthen their alliance.Later, Rahul Gandhi will interact with students at Island Grounds as part of the Congress’s nationwide ‘Voice of Students’ (Manavargalin Kural) campaign. This will be his sixth such interaction under the initiative, which aims to highlight issues affecting students and young people.He is expected to speak about question paper leaks, unemployment, alleged exploitation by coaching centres, examination-related irregularities, declining allocations for education and concerns over student safety.
Article Summary: The meeting comes a day after the TVK-led front won its first electoral test, retaining the Madurantakam and Dharapuram assembly constituencies in the October 6 bypolls. The meeting also comes against the backdrop of protests demanding the removal of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.

Article Title: Mahatma Gandhi’s great-grandson, Tushar Gandhi detained in Mumbai
Article Text:
Activist Tushar Gandhi was taken into custody by Mumbai police just before a planned demonstration at August Kranti Maidan

Mumbai Police cites lack of permission for protest

CJP protest targets CEC Gyanesh Kumar over SIR





MUMBAI: Mumbai Police on Saturday detained activist Tushar Gandhi and others ahead of a proposed demonstration at August Kranti Maidan in solidarity with the Cockroach Janta Party’s ( CJP ) protest against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar at Delhi’s Jantar Mantar.Tushar Gandhi, the great-grandson of Mahatma Gandhi and head of the organisation ‘Hum Bharat Ke Log’, was picked up from Bandra and taken to DN Nagar police station, an official said.Gandhi had shared a poster on X urging citizens to join a protest gathering at August Kranti Maidan at 3.30pm.Activist Feeroz Mithiborwala was also taken into custody from his residence and shifted to the MIDC police station, officials said.The detentions came ahead of the proposed demonstration, which was organised in solidarity with the CJP’s planned mobilisation at Jantar Mantar against alleged irregularities in the electoral process.Ahead of the proposed gathering, Zonal Deputy Commissioner of Police Ragasudha R said no application seeking permission for the event had been submitted to Gamdevi police station and no official approval had been granted.Authorities said August Kranti Maidan is not a designated protest site under a Bombay High Court order. Police took preventive action to maintain law and order ahead of the proposed demonstration.The CJP has called for a demonstration at Jantar Mantar against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over allegations of voter-list manipulation during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and changes relating to Form 6, which is used for voter registration.More than 1,500 people have been detained from several parts of Delhi ahead of the Cockroach Janta Party’s (CJP) proposed protest at Jantar Mantar against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, as police intensified preventive measures across the national capital.(With PTI inputs)
Article Summary: Tushar Gandhi, the great-grandson of Mahatma Gandhi, was picked up from Bandra and taken to DN Nagar police station. Gandhi had shared a poster on X urging citizens to join a protest gathering at August Kranti Maidan at 3.30pm.

Article Title: Two more arrested in Shiv Sena (UBT) man’s murder case
Article Text:
Pradeep Purnekar

Thane:





The Special Investigation Team (SIT) probing Shiv Sena (UBT) functionary Pradeep Purnekar’s murder case has arrested two more accused, Amit Jaykishan Singh alias Paplu (34), an autorickshaw driver from Bhayandar East, and Santosh Mehialal Kanojia alias Talli (41), a laundry operator from Manpada, Kapurbawdi, Thane.Both hail from Varanasi district in Uttar Pradesh.Police said that the two accused are believed to be the main conspirators.Meanwhile, accused Papya Shinde was remanded in police custody till Oct 12 after investigators told a Thane court that he had allegedly supplied firearms, weapons and multiple SIM cards to the other accused.Senior police inspector Shailesh Salvi of Crime Branch’s Anti-Extortion Cell and also the investigating officer of SIT told the court on Friday that Shinde had allegedly provided a mobile phone to Kanojia. He had also allegedly supplied multiple SIM cards to the other accused, and investigators are probing their source and whether they were procured using different identities.Salvi told the court that Shinde was in contact with the other accused and had allegedly supplied weapons owing to his strong financial position. He said Shinde was not cooperating with investigators and sought four more days of police custody to establish the source of the firearms, trace the communication network and gather further evidence.The investigating team has recovered one of the two firearms allegedly supplied by Shinde, along with a mobile phone and a vehicle, the court was told.The complainant’s lawyer Sameer Hatle submitted that Shinde had allegedly supplied two firearms and other weapons to the accused. He also raised the possibility of political links in the supply of the firearms and questioned whether political figures had provided the weapons.Opposing the police custody plea, the defence lawyer argued that Shinde had cooperated with the investigation and had already spent 10 days in police custody. The defence further submitted that certain political figures had allegedly been named by other accused during questioning but had not yet been interrogated.After hearing the arguments, Judge S B Sable remanded Shinde in police custody till Oct 12 to enable investigators to pursue further leads in the murder case.
Article Summary: SIT probing Shiv Sena functionary Pradeep Purnekar’s murder case has arrested two more accused. Amit Jaykishan Singh alias Paplu and Santosh Mehialal Kanojia alias Talli hail from Varanasi district in Uttar Pradesh. Police said that the two accused are believed to be the main conspirators.

Article Title: Visually impaired Beed girl bags MBBS seat after HC intervention
Article Text:
Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar:





An 18-year-old visually impaired girl from Beed, initially declared unfit to study medicine, has secured an MBBS seat after a legal battle in the Bombay High Court. The court’s intervention led to a fresh functional assessment that found her competent to pursue medical education.Syeda Musfira Fatema Rafiuddin has now been admitted to Govt Medical College, Sangli-Miraj.Musfira has congenital low vision caused by albinism, nystagmus and amblyopia. She scored 345 out of 720 in NEET-UG 2026 and secured an All-India OBC-NCL PwBD rank of 796.Her medical aspirations, however, hit a roadblock on Aug 10. The Medical Assessment Board at Sir JJ Group of Hospitals, Mumbai, declared her “ineligible for pursuing medical education”. It cited her visual condition and dependence on low-vision assistive devices.Musfira challenged the decision before the Aurangabad bench of the Bombay high court. Her counsel, advocate Sayyed Tauseef Yaseen, argued before a division bench of Justice Nitin B Suryawanshi and Justice Abasaheb D Shinde that the medical board had merely recorded her diagnosis.It had not conducted a functional or task-based assessment or considered reasonable accommodation, he submitted.Yaseen relied on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016, and the Supreme Court judgment in Omkar Ramchandra Gond v Union of India. He argued that Musfira had already demonstrated her ability by competing in a rigorous national-level examination with prescribed magnifying aids. Her functional ability, rather than merely her diagnosis, should, therefore, have been assessed, he submitted.With NEET counselling underway, HC on Sept 22 directed Musfira to approach the appellate forum at Madras Medical College, Chennai, for an urgent reassessment.After evaluating her functional ability with low-vision aids, the appellate forum on Sept 25 declared her eligible and competent to pursue medical education under the PwBD category.A technical issue on the counselling portal then prevented Musfira from opting for the PwBD category. Yaseen approached the high court again on Sept 28. The authorities subsequently undertook to reopen the registration window for Musfira and facilitate her participation in the All-India and state counselling processes.She was subsequently allotted an MBBS seat at Govt Medical College, Sangli-Miraj, and granted admission.On Oct 1, Yaseen informed the high court that Musfira had secured admission. The bench then disposed of her petition as infructuous.
Article Summary: Syeda Musfira Fatema Rafiuddin has congenital low vision caused by albinism, nystagmus and amblyopia. She scored 345 out of 720 in NEET-UG 2026 and secured an All-India OBC-NCL PwBD rank of 796. The Medical Assessment Board at Sir JJ Group of Hospitals, Mumbai, declared her ‘ineligible for pursuing medical education’

Article Title: Three corner contest for Pune graduates, Sena relents makes teachers poll between BJP and Cong
Article Text:
MVA leaders with graduates candidate Harshada Jadhav and teachers candidate Jayant Asgaonkar

Kolhapur





: Shiv Sena (UBT) has declined to withdraw its candidate, Sunil Modi, who filed his nomination for Pune Graduates’ MLC seat. According to Modi, party chief Uddhav Thackeray has already instructed local cadres to begin the campaign.Friday marked the final deadline for withdrawal of nominations for graduates’ and teachers’ constituency MLC elections.A consensus could not be reached within Maha Vikas Aghadi (MVA). Explaining the situation to TOI, Modi said, “The seat was left to our party. However, since a consensus could not be reached, we decided to contest the seat. I have spoken to our party chief, who has asked the organisation to support and campaign for me.”Consequently, Pune Graduates’ seat will see a triangular fight. Harshada Jadhav is contesting as the official candidate of NCP (SP), while Dr Smita Jadhav is in the fray as the official candidate of BJP . Meanwhile, NCP rebel Pratap alias Bhaiya Mane withdrew his nomination. Mane said he withdrew at the request of his leader, minister Hasan Mushrif. Interestingly, Mane had earlier approached NCP (SP) chief Sharad Pawar for a ticket, but Pawar declined, stating he no longer trusted leaders from Kagal— the taluka in Kolhapur to which both Mushrif and Mane belong.On the other hand, Mangesh Chivate, the candidate from Eknath Shinde ’s Shiv Sena, withdrew from the race for the Pune Teachers’ constituency. The BJP has nominated Kaustubh Gawade for the seat, who will now face a direct contest against the sitting MLC, Jayant Asgaonkar of Congress , who also hails from Kolhapur. Following his withdrawal, Chivate noted that in his party, the orders of party chief— deputy chief minister Eknath Shinde—are strictly followed, and he complied without questioning the underlying reasons.Sources revealed that CM Devendra Fadnavis and DCM Eknath Shinde held discussions to resolve the impasse. While both leaders initially tried to convince each other, neither relented until the final moments, when Shinde ultimately chose not to stretch the alliance’s friction further and instructed Chivate to pull out.Meanwhile, campaigning has officially begun for the graduates’ constituency. NCP (SP) MLA Jayant Patil, Congress MLA Vishwajeet Kadam, and Sangli MP Vishal Patil have endorsed Harshada Jadhav, urging their supporters to connect with registered graduate voters and secure their support.State BJP president Ravindra Chavan claimed on Friday that the remaining internal differences within Mahayuti alliance over the Pune MLC seats will soon be resolved. While kickstarting the campaign in Pune for alliance candidates Smita Jadhav and Kaustubh Gawade, Chavan told the media: “We will contest this election as a united Mahayuti. Our senior leader Chandrakant Patil will hold a meeting with Mahayuti coordinators from western Maharashtra to iron out any differences and ensure workers from all three alliance parties campaign together. ”(Inputs from Anurag Bende in Pune)
Article Summary: Friday marked the final deadline for withdrawal of nominations for graduates’ and teachers’ constituency MLC elections. Shiv Sena (UBT) has declined to withdraw its candidate, Sunil Modi, who filed his nomination for Pune Graduates’ MLC seat. A consensus could not be reached within Maha Vikas Aghadi (MVA)

Article Title: Congress MLC & Mahayuti-led panel announce candidates for Gokul polls
Article Text:
Satej Patil announces Samvichari panel candidates for Gokul Dairy election

Kolhapur

:





Two coalition panels on Thursday announced 25 candidates each for elections in Kolhapur District Cooperative Milk Producers Federation, popularly known as Gokul Dairy.In Mahayuti-led Chhatrapati Shahu Shetkari Vikas Aghadi, the prominent candidates are BJP’s Shoumika Mahadik, minister Hasan Mushrif’s son Navid Mushrif, former MLA Sujit Minchekar and Rajesh Patil. Most of the candidates have served as directors of Gokul Dairy in the past.On the other hand, Congress MLC Satej Patil-led Rajarshi Shahu Shetkari Samvichari Aghadi has announced prominent candidates such as Shashikant Patil Chuyekar, son of the founder of Gokul Dairy, Anandrao Patil Chuyekar, former MLA Raju Awale, former Kolhapur ZP vice-president Shashikant Khot and most of the candidates are associated with cooperative institutions.The announcement of ‘Samvichari Aghadi’ was held in the presence of Patil, ex-MP Raju Shetti, Peasants and Workers Party leader Jayant Patil, Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Vijay Devane and NCP(SP)’s VB Patil. Satej Patil also announced the manifesto of Samvichari Aghadi, which will be taken to around 5,300 voters who are delegates of the primary milk societies. “We have decided to increase Gokul Dairy’s collection of milk from 20 lakh litres per day to 30 lakh litres per day.We would increase the price by at least Rs5 per litre for buffalo milk and Rs2 per litre for cow milk. Also, the price of cattle feed would be reduced by Rs 100 per sack within the first month,” said Patil.Patil announced that Shashikant Patil Chuyekar would be made chairperson of Gokul if Samvichari Aghadi gets a majority.Raju Shetti said CM Devendra Fadnavis ’s flagship Nagpur-Goa Shaktipeeth Expressway project will be one of the key issues over which the election for Gokul will be fought. “The highway would destroy the rural economy. Sugarcane crop would suffer, followed by the industries that depend on it,” said Shetti.The panels will get their symbols on Friday. The voting is scheduled for Oct 18.
Article Summary: Two coalition panels on Thursday announced 25 candidates each for elections in Kolhapur District Cooperative Milk Producers Federation.
