Article Title: Rs 1 lakh bribe trap: Navi Mumbai ACB catches circle officer, talathi and woman assistant
Article Text:
The arrested accused were identified as Keshav Dagdu Mohite, Jaihind Birsha Koli (49) and Monika Vijnesh Patil (36).





NAVI MUMBAI: The Navi Mumbai Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) has arrested two revenue officials and a woman assistant for allegedly accepting a Rs 1 lakh bribe from a villager in Chirner, Uran taluka, to register the names of his relatives in the 7/12 extract of a land record.The arrested accused were identified as Keshav Dagdu Mohite (52), circle officer at Koproli in Uran taluka; Jaihind Birsha Koli (49), talathi; and Monika Vijnesh Patil (36), an assistant to the revenue officials.Dharmaraj Sonake, deputy superintendent of police, Navi Mumbai ACB, said the complainant had applied to register the names of the heirs of his deceased sister in the 7/12 extract of their land in Chirner.The land was jointly owned by the complainant's maternal uncle, aunt, brother and sister. The complainant had also applied for deletion of his deceased brother's name and submitted the request to circle officer Mohite and talathi Koli. However, the two officials allegedly demanded Rs 1 lakh from him to process the work.Dy SP Sonake said, "After verification of the complaint on Monday, when it was confirmed that the revenue officers Mohite and Koli had told the complainant to hand over the bribe amount to the accused woman assistant Monika Patil, a trap was laid on Tuesday around 2 pm. After the woman assistant Monika Patil accepted the demanded bribe of Rs 1 lakh from the complainant and handed it over to circle officer Keshav Mohite, both were caught red-handed and arrested. While, the acccused Talathi Jaihind Koli who was involved in the bribe demand was taken into custody from Dronagiri."
Article Summary: The Navi Mumbai Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) has arrested two revenue officials and a woman assistant for allegedly accepting a Rs 1 lakh bribe. The arrested accused were identified as Keshav Dagdu Mohite (52), circle officer at Koproli in Uran taluka; Jaihind Birsha Koli (49), talathi; and Monika Vijnesh Patil (36)

Article Title: Man in Mahindra Thar with duplicate plate molests woman, knocks down another in Kharghar
Article Text:
30-year-old man was apprehended for allegedly molesting a woman and injuring another in Navi Mumbai.





NAVI MUMBAI: A 30-year-old man wearing a mask and driving a red Thar SUV with a duplicate registration number plate was apprehended by the Crime Branch Unit-3 team within 10 hours on Thursday evening.He had allegedly molested a 26-year-old woman walking on the street in Kharghar, around 400metres from Pethpada metro station, on September 30 night and, an hour later, severely injured a 22-year-old woman by knocking her down in Belpada, Sector 3, Kharghar.Acting on a complaint by the woman allegedly molested by the Thar SUV driver, Kharghar police registered an FIR under BNS section 74 for the offence of assault or criminal force against a woman with the intent to outrage her modesty.While, as per the complaint by the injured woman Shrawani Dandekar, a resident of sector 3, Belpada, an FIR under relevant BNS sections and Motor Vehicle Act was registered against the Thar SUV driver for rash and negligent driving causing hurt.The detained aaccused identified as Ali alias Talib Ahsan Nakhvi, a resident of sector 50, Seawoods, Nerul was handed over to Kharghar police for further legal action.Previously, in January 2021, he was arrested by Nerul police in the FIR registered against him for alleged kidnapping, sexual harassment and molestation of a woman.Sanjay Joshi, senior inspector of Kharghar said, "The accused Nakhvi has been detained and subsequently it will be decided whether to arrest him or serve with a notice under Bharatiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) for cooperating in police investigating."Audumbar Patil, senior inspector of crime branch unit-3 said, "After an FIR for molestation was registered at Kharghar police station by the victim woman, a resident of sector 34, Kharghar. As per the orders of higher authority, our team started a parallel probe. From the CCTV camera surveillance near the crime scene, we obtained the red Thar SUV's registration number, which was of Vashi RTO passing.""When verified, the registration number was found to be that of a Maruti WagonR car. As the accused had used a duplicate registration number plate, we scrutinized as many as 62 Thar SUVs registered with various Regional Transport Offices (RTOs). Subsequently, we obtained the registration number of a red Thar SUV that was registered with Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar RTO," Patil added.SPI Patil further informed, "The SUV was registered in the name of Ali alias Talib Ahsan Nakhvi, a resident of Devaki Apartment in sector-50, Seawoods. From his mobile number registered with the RTO, his location was tracked.""He was apprehended from Bonkode village, Koparkhairane on Thursday late evening. Upon thorough interrogation, he confessed that he had inappropriately touched the woman pedestrian near Pethpada metro station while he drove his Thar SUV and sped away. He even confessed to have injured a woman pedestrian by hitting her his SUV while driving in Belpada area," he said.
Article Summary: A 30-year-old man wearing a mask and driving a red Thar SUV with a duplicate registration number plate was apprehended by the Crime Branch Unit-3 team on Thursday evening. He had allegedly molested a woman walking on the street in Kharghar, around 400metres from Pethpada metro station, on September 30 night. An hour later, he severely injured a woman by knocking her down in Belpada, Sector 3, KharGHar.

Article Title: 2 women escape from RPF lockup in Navi Mumbai; 1 held after 6 hours, cop suspended
Article Text:
The women removed their sarees, tied one end to the generator on the balcony and climbed down before escaping. (AI image)





NAVI MUMBAI: In a major security lapse at Belapur Railway Protection Force (RPF), two women arrested for allegedly attempting to steal overhead electric wires from the Juinagar railway godown escaped from the lockup after midnight on September 28.One of them was apprehended around six hours later, while the other remains at large.The woman constable on night duty has been suspended and a departmental inquiry has been initiated against her.As per the FIR registered by RPF sub-inspector Milap Parte (52) at Panvel GRP, a case was registered on September 24 under Section 3(a) of the Railway Property (Unauthorized Possession) Act, 1966, Amendment 2012, at Belapur railway police station.The case was based on a written memo submitted by RPF personnel Ravikant Gade regarding the theft of overhead electric wires from the godown at Juinagar railway station on September 21.During the probe, a trap was laid on September 26 and around 1pm, two women were found loitering suspiciously near the Juinagar godown with the alleged intention of committing theft.They were taken into custody and identified as Rupali Kailas Kurhade (30), from Jalna, and Shalibai Ashok Pawar (49), from Bhiwandi.They were arrested after an FIR was registered for attempted theft and produced before a CSMT court, which remanded them to police custody till September 30. They were lodged in the lockup at Belapur RPF police station.Day-shift woman constable Rakhi Malaiya was assigned guard duty at the lockup, after which woman head constable Pooja Bagre was on night duty.Around 2am on September 28, when Bagre had gone to the toilet, the two women allegedly managed to open the lock by inserting their hands through the iron bars of the lockup and jerking it. Police suspect the lock may not have been secured properly.The women then reached the balcony at the rear end of the police station. They removed their sarees, tied one end to the generator on the balcony and climbed down before escaping.The incident was captured on CCTV footage. PSI Parte learnt about the escape after waking up at home around 6.30am and finding several missed calls from head constable Bagre and ASI Rajiv Parsan.Sunil Nila, chief spokesperson of Central Railway, said, "One accused woman Rupali Kurhade was apprehended from near Nerul railway station around 8.45 am. The other accused Shalibai Pawar is still absconding."
Article Summary: The women removed their sarees, tied one end to the generator on the balcony and climbed down before escaping. One of them was apprehended around six hours later, while the other remains at large. The woman constable on night duty has been suspended and a departmental inquiry has been initiated.

Article Title: Thane Shiv Sena (UBT) leader murder: 2 more arrested near Alibag while fleeing to Goa, total 3
Article Text:
Two additional suspects were arrested in connection with the murder of Shiv Sena division chief Pradeep Purnekar.





THANE: The Thane Crime Branch has arrested two more accused in connection with the murder of Shiv Sena (UBT) division chief Pradeep alias Balu Purnekar, taking the total number of arrests in the case to three.The arrested accused have been identified as Nikhil Yadav and Nitesh Pawar alias Bhavdya. The two were apprehended near Alibag while allegedly attempting to flee towards Goa, according to police sources.The Crime Branch reportedly traced the duo following information obtained during the questioning of suspects detained earlier in the case. Police teams had been searching for the accused after Purnekar was shot and attacked with a sharp-edged weapon at his office in Thane.According to investigators, Yadav allegedly opened fire on Purnekar, while Pawar allegedly attacked him with a sharp weapon. Police are now expected to question both accused to establish the sequence of events, the motive and the role of others involved in the alleged conspiracy.The two accused are expected to be produced before the Thane Sessions Court on Friday. Police will also attempt to recover the weapons allegedly used in the murder and investigate how the accused obtained them.Earlier, Prakash alias Papya Shinde was arrested in connection with the case. The police have also formed a Special Investigation Team (SIT) headed by DCP (Crime) Amarsingh Jadhav to conduct a detailed probe into the killing.The investigation is continuing, with police probing the alleged conspiracy, the role of other suspects and the possible involvement of the absconding accused.
Article Summary: The arrested accused have been identified as Nikhil Yadav and Nitesh Pawar alias Bhavdya. The two were apprehended near Alibag while allegedly attempting to flee towards Goa. Police are now expected to question both accused to establish the sequence of events, the motive and the role of others involved.

Article Title: Disha Salian case: Father, lawyer seek police protection, allege threats from Sena (UBT) leaders
Article Text:
Ojha questioned Aaditya Thackeray’s ‘Y-plus’ security, saying those who raised the issue and allegedly faced threats remained unprotected.

(With agency inputs)





THANE: Advocate Nilesh Ojha on Sunday said that Disha Salian’s father, Satish Salian, Sameer Wankhede, Ashutosh Pathak and he have sought police protection, alleging that they received threats from Shiv Sena (UBT) leaders.Ojha, who is representing Satish Salian in the case, said they have written to Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Union home minister Amit Shah, the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI), the Chief Justice of India and Maharashtra chief minister Devendra Fadnavis, seeking protection."The CBI FIR was registered, and a letter was immediately written requesting police protection for four individuals: Satish Salian, our witness Sameer Wankhede, myself, and Ashutosh Pathak, " Ojha told news agency ANI.Ojha questioned the provision of ‘Y-plus’ security to Aaditya Thackeray , saying those who brought the matter to light and allegedly faced threats had been left without protection."The letter clearly states, citing records from your Home Ministry and the Narcotics Bureau, that it is evident that Aditya Thackeray is involved in the drug trade. Furthermore, an FIR has now been registered against him regarding gang rape, murder, and a cover-up.Several other high-profile individuals and police officers are also implicated as accused in this matter," he said."We have already provided all prima facie evidence; the CBI has obtained everything necessary during the investigation to secure a conviction. Yet, the accused currently enjoys 'Y-plus' security provided by your administration. Meanwhile, those who brought this matter to light and those facing direct threats from individuals like Sanjay Raut were left unprotected," the advocate added.He further said that providing security was mandatory under the Witness Protection Scheme and Supreme Court guidelines, and alleged that their request for protection had not been acted upon.He further added, "Providing security is mandatory under the Witness Protection Scheme and Supreme Court guidelines. Yet, they failed to do so. Consequently, we compiled all the material and handed it over to the CBI. We also urged them to investigate the role of Police Commissioner Deven Bharti and determine why police protection was not granted.""We have given a copy of this to the CBI, along with Prime Minister Modi ji, the Home Minister, the Chief Justice of India, and the Chief Minister," Ojha said.Disha Salian was found dead in Mumbai on June 8, 2020. Her death was initially registered as an Accidental Death Report (ADR).Salian died days before actor Sushant Singh Rajput , whose death also led to a high-profile investigation and widespread public controversy.Bombay High Court directed the CBI to register a formal First Information Report (FIR) and launch a fresh probe.As the probe progresses, Satish Salian, accompanied by his lawyer Nilesh Ojha, has submitted a pen drive containing material they described as evidence related to Disha Salian’s death.Meanwhile, Aaditya Thackeray has denied the allegations and responded to the defamation notice issued by Satish Salian.
Article Summary: Disha Salian’s father, Satish Salian, Sameer Wankhede, Ashutosh Pathak and he have sought police protection. They allege that they received threats from Shiv Sena (UBT) leaders. Ojha questioned the provision of ‘Y-plus’ security to Aaditya Thackeray. He said those who raised the issue and allegedly faced threats remained unprotected.

Article Title: Woman alleges Pune animal shelter refused to return her 7 dogs, demands Rs3.5 lakh
Article Text:
Representative image

Pune:





The founder and a trustee of an animal rescue and shelter centre allegedly refused to return a woman’s seven dogs. Instead, the duo demanded Rs3.5 lakh from her to return them.Lohegaon police on Thursday registered a case against the duo under sections 314 (dishonest misappropriation of property) and 316 (criminal breach of trust) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).The 39-year-old woman, a resident of Lohegaon, stated in her complaint that she had temporarily left her seven dogs at the shelter in January this year. However, when she sought their return, the shelter’s office-bearers allegedly refused to hand them over. “The woman alleged that the founder and the trustee abused her. They also demanded Rs3.5 lakh from her and threatened her,” an officer from Lohegaon police said.Police are investigating further.
Article Summary: The 39-year-old woman, a resident of Lohegaon, stated in her complaint that she had temporarily left her seven dogs at the shelter in January this year. When she sought their return, the shelter’s office-bearers allegedly refused to hand them over.

Article Title: Two siblings held on charge of stabbing fabrication worker to death after row over damaged shoes in bikes’ collision in Ahilyanagar
Article Text:
The arrested siblings have been remanded in police custody till Oct 12

Nashik:





Two siblings were arrested from Mumbai on Thursday for allegedly stabbing to death a 55-year-old fabrication worker as shoes of one of them was damaged after their motorcycle brushed the victim’s two-wheeler on Balikashram Road in Ahilyanagar on Wednesday evening.The deceased fabrication worker was identified as Ravindra Rambhau Chavan (55), a resident of Bhingardive Mala at Bhutkarwadi in Savedi, Ahilyanagar. The arrested siblings, Suraj Ravi Sonawane and Prem alias Sonulya Ravi Sonawane from Siddharthnagar in Ahilyanagar, were produced before a court and remanded in police custody till Oct 12.Tofkhana police registered a case of murder against Suraj and Sonulya under relevant sections of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023, and the Arms Act, 1959, based on a complaint filed by the victim’s son, Manthan Ravindra Chavan (25).Police said the victim, Ravindra, was riding the motorcycle around 5pm on Wednesday with an acquaintance, Mikhail Shankar Bhakare. Their two-wheeler slightly sideswiped the motorcycle of the accused. The shoes of one of the riders of the other motorcycle was damaged in the minor collision and an argument broke out over it.Inspector Balaji Vaidya of Tofkhana police said the accused duo allegedly attacked Ravindra with sharp weapons in the course of the altercation and inflicted severe injuries on his back and left arm. Bhakare immediately alerted the victim’s family about the latter’s injury over the phone. Ravindra was rushed to Civil Hospital in Ahilyanagar, where attending doctors declared him dead on arrival.
Article Summary: The deceased fabrication worker was identified as Ravindra Rambhau Chavan (55), a resident of Bhingardive Mala at Bhutkarwadi in Savedi, Ahilyanagar. The arrested siblings, Suraj Ravi Sonawane and Prem alias Sonulya RaviSonawane, were produced before a court and remanded in police custody till Oct 12.

Article Title: CPM condemns Centre’s crackdown on CJP protesters, announces demonstrations across Tamil Nadu
Article Text:
CPM P. Shanmugam





CHENNAI: The CPM on Saturday strongly condemned the Union government’s crackdown, including the alleged siege of Left party offices and the detention of senior leaders on their way to participate in the CJP protest at Jantar Mantar in Delhi. The protest demanded the immediate removal of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.Condemning the alleged assault on democratic rights and the detention of senior leaders and students, the party announced demonstrations at all district headquarters across Tamil Nadu.According to a post on X, the CJP’s protest at Jantar Mantar received widespread support from various political parties, student groups and youth organisations. However, the Union government allegedly resorted to severe repressive measures, deploying Delhi Police and paramilitary forces. Left party offices were placed under siege, and protesters were prevented from gathering, the post claimed.Several senior Left leaders were detained while on their way to the venue. Those detained included CPM general secretary MA Baby, CPI general secretary D Raja, CPI(ML) leaders, Politburo members Pinarayi Vijayan and U Vasuki, Tamil Nadu state secretary P Shanmugam, and Central Committee member John Brittas.In what the party described as an attempt to intimidate protesters, Delhi Police allegedly kept the detained leaders, including former Kerala chief minister Pinarayi Vijayan, inside police vehicles and drove them around the capital for more than an hour without formally processing their detention.Strongly condemning the police action and what it described as the suppression of democratic dissent, the CPI(M) announced immediate demonstrations at all district headquarters across Tamil Nadu, demanding an end to the Union government’s coercive measures.
Article Summary: The CPM condemned the Union government’s crackdown, including the alleged siege of Left party offices and the detention of senior leaders. The protest demanded the immediate removal of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Those detained included CPM general secretary MA Baby, CPI general secretary D Raja and CPI(ML) leaders.

Article Title: TVK’s P Sathyabama wins Dharapuram byelection; Vijay party's Maragatham Kumaravel extends her lead in Madurantakam
Article Text:
TVK candidate P Sathyabama with party president and Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay





COIMBATORE/CHENNAI: TVK candidate P Sathyabama on Friday won the Dharapuram byelection by a margin of 9,471 votes, securing 66,841 votes.DMK candidate S Suganya came second with 57,370 votes, while AIADMK's K Banumathi secured 45,280 votes.The bypoll was necessitated after Sathyabama, who had won Dharapuram seat as an AIADMK candidate in the April assembly election, resigned as MLAs and joined the ruling TVK.Meanwhile, at the of 16th round of counting of votes in Madurantakam , TVK candidate Maragatham Kumaravel secured 63,391 votes, extending her lead over DMK candidate I Paranthaman (46,086 votes) to 17,305 votes. AIADMK candidate Kanitha Sampath remained in third place with 41,133 votes.Maragatham, who had won the Madurantakam seat as an AIADMK candidate in the last assembly election, resigned as MLAs and joined the ruling TVK, like Sathyabama.Polling was held in Dharapuram and Madurantakam on Oct 6.
Article Summary: TVK candidate P Sathyabama on Friday won the Dharapuram byelection by a margin of 9,471 votes, securing 66,841 votes. DMK candidate S Suganya came second with 57,370 votes, while AIADMK's K Banumathi secured 45,280 votes.

Article Title: Dharapuram bypoll: EVMs, VVPATs secured under two-tier armed cover, 24x7 CCTV surveillance
Article Text:
Representative image





TIRUPUR: Electronic voting machines (EVMs) and voter verifiable paper audit trail (VVPAT) units used for the Dharapuram assembly byelection in Tirupur district have been placed in a strong room under two-tier armed security and round-the-clock CCTV surveillance, officials said.After the completion of polling on Oct 6, the EVMs and VVPAT units were brought to the counting centre located at LRG Govt Women’s Arts College in the district.District election officer and collector Dr Manish Narnaware and election general observer Chinmay Pundlikrao Gotmare, IAS, on Wednesday supervised the placement of machines into the strong room in the presence of candidates and their agents. The strong room was sealed thereafter, with the participation of superintendent of police Srishti Singh, IPS, deputy commissioner of police Akash Joshi, IPS, and Dharapuram revenue divisional officer A Felix Raja.Narnaware said the strong room would be opened on Oct 9 -- the counting day -- in the presence of candidates or their representatives and the central observer, under videography.District election authorities said the strong room was being protected with armed security personnel in a two-tier arrangement, with continuous monitoring through CCTV cameras.To ensure uninterrupted supervision of CCTV feeds, three officers of deputy collector rank have been deployed daily at the district level, while separate monitoring officers have been appointed for the assembly constituency.The monitoring will continue until the counting day on Oct 9.Authorities said all contesting candidates have been informed in writing about appointing representatives to observe the security arrangements, with permission granted for such representatives to stay outside the inner security cordon.Polling was held at 320 booths in the constituency. There are 2,23,306 registered voters, and 1,79,214 votes were cast, recording a turnout of 80.25%.
Article Summary: Electronic voting machines used for Dharapuram assembly byelection in Tirupur district. EVMs and VVPAT units placed in strong room under two-tier armed security and round-the-clock CCTV surveillance. The monitoring will continue until the counting day on Oct 9.

Article Title: 864 bottles of liquor seized from house near Erode; man arrested
Article Text: ERODE: Police seized 864 bottles of Indian made foreign liquor (IMFL) from a house near Mylambadi in Erode district in the early hours of Thursday and arrested a man.Acting on a tip-off that bottles of liquor had been illegally stored for unauthorised sale, the Bhavani police conducted a raid at the house of K Govindaraj, 28, of Ammapalayam. They found 864 bottles of IMFL stocked in the house for illegal sale.Police registered a case and arrested Govindaraj. He was remanded in judicial custody.They launched a search for Sekar alias Ammasai, 34, and Sridhar, 38, who have links with the illegal liquor operation.
Article Summary: Police seized 864 bottles of Indian made foreign liquor (IMFL) from a house near Mylambadi in Erode district. Acting on a tip-off that bottles of liquor had been illegally stored for unauthorised sale, the Bhavani police conducted a raid.

Article Title: Death sentence on preacher for sexual assault on minor girls referred to HC
Article Text:
Death sentence on preacher for sexual assault on minor girls referred to HC

Madurai

:





The death sentence imposed on a preacher for sexually assaulting four minor girls in Tirunelveli was referred to Madras high court for confirmation on Thursday.The case of the prosecution is that Abraham, 47, a preacher, sexually assaulted the girls at his church, during music classes and at deserted places in their neighbourhood. The abuse came to light in 2022 after an eight-year-old girl complained of pain in her private parts. Her mother took her to a hospital, where she learnt that the child had been sexually assaulted.Three other girls from the same extended family told their mothers that Abraham had also sexually assaulted them from the Covid-19 lockdown in 2020 to 2022. In 2022, police registered a case for offences under Pocso Act and arrested Abraham.In August, the special court for exclusive trial of cases under Pocso Act in Tirunelveli convicted Abraham and imposed the death sentence on him. Since the death sentence was imposed by the trial court, the same was referred to HC for confirmation.A division bench of Justice M Nirmal Kumar and Justice N Gunasekaran posted the referred trial case for hearing on October 30.
Article Summary: The case of the prosecution is that Abraham, 47, a preacher, sexually assaulted the girls at his church, during music classes and at deserted places in their neighbourhood. The abuse came to light in 2022 after an eight-year-old girl complained of pain in her private parts. In 2022, police registered a case for offences under Pocso Act and arrested Abraham.

Article Title: Four held with ₹2 lakh counterfeit currency in Madurai
Article Text: Madurai: Four men were arrested after police seized counterfeit ₹500 notes worth ₹2 lakh during a vehicle check near Pudupatti tank bund on Thursday. Police said the suspects, travelling in an autorickshaw, tried to flee on spotting officers. The notes carried identical serial numbers and were intended for circulation. Those arrested were Premkumar , 50, Christopher Mathiyazhagan, 32, Karthik , 32, and Maheswaran, 35. Police also seized a computer, printer and chemicals allegedly used to produce the counterfeit currency.
Article Summary: The notes carried identical serial numbers and were intended for circulation. Police also seized a computer, printer and chemicals allegedly used to produce the counterfeit currency. Those arrested were Premkumar, 50, Christopher Mathiyazhagan, 32, Karthik, 32, and Maheswaran, 35.

Article Title: Traffic affected on Salem-Madurai National Highway after trailer truck crashes near Rasipuram
Article Text: NAMAKKAL: Traffic was affected for more than an hour on the Salem-Madurai National Highway near Rasipuram in Namakkal district on Thursday afternoon after a trailer truck crashed while descending the Andagalur Gate flyover.No casualties or injuries were reported.The truck was carrying about 60 tonnes of steel angles from Maharashtra to Karur. An officer at the Rasipuram police station said the driver lost control of the vehicle while descending the flyover around 1.30pm. The truck hit a streetlight pole on the roadside. “The vehicle partially blocked the road, causing congestion and delays for motorists and commuters,” he said.Vehicles piled up for two kilometres on the NH. The Rasipuram police reached the spot after receiving information, regulated traffic and moved the truck to the roadside.Police registered a case and were investigating the circumstances leading to the crash.
Article Summary: Trailer truck crashes on Salem-Madurai National Highway near Rasipuram. Truck was carrying 60 tonnes of steel angles from Maharashtra to Karur. Driver lost control of the vehicle while descending the flyover. No casualties or injuries were reported.

Article Title: CMRL pay-off case: Kerala High Court orders FIR against Pinarayi, Veena, Riyas
Article Text:
Pinarayi Vijayan

Kochi:





Kerala High Court on Friday directed the vigilance director to register an FIR against former chief minister Pinarayi Vijayan , his daughter T Veena and her husband, former minister P A Mohamed Riyas, under Prevention of Corruption Act over the alleged CMRL-Exalogic pay-off without delay.The HC also set aside the state police chief’s order constituting a special investigation team (SIT) to conduct a preliminary inquiry into the matter based on inputs from Enforcement Directorate (ED), instead of registering a case. Justice A Badharudeen gave the order on a petition filed by K M Shajahan, a political activist from Thiruvananthapuram, seeking a directive to the vigilance director to register a case. Shajahan alleged that the preliminary inquiry was intended to protect the corrupt.The HC observed that ED’s communication contained sufficient material to register a case, including statements of witnesses and suspected persons and other evidence beyond the notebooks and diaries. It, therefore, held that a preliminary inquiry by an SIT was unnecessary.The court directed the DGP/SIT head to hand over the information and details provided by ED to the vigilance director. It also directed ED to forward all necessary documents to the vigilance department, which should investigate the allegations with competent officers and file the final report without undue delay.The case arose from an ED communication to the state police chief under Section 66(2) of the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA), recommending the registration of a case under the Prevention of Corruption Act. ED alleged that CMRL had paid Rs 3.28 crore to Exalogic Solutions, a defunct company owned by Veena, without receiving corresponding IT consultancy services. Instead of registering a case, the DGP constituted the SIT headed by crime branch SP Vikraman P to conduct a preliminary inquiry into the veracity of the allegations.Advocate general K Jaju Babu defended the preliminary inquiry, arguing that the state govt had a duty to balance the allegations against the rights of the suspected persons. He also pointed out that the Muvattupuzha special court and the HC had earlier dismissed petitions filed by the late Gireesh Babu of Kalamassery seeking an investigation into the same allegations. The HC had dismissed another petition filed by MLA Mathew Kuzhalnadan seeking the same relief, and the Supreme Court had upheld the decision.The HC, however, noted that several materials referred to in ED’s communication had been collected after the earlier petitions were dismissed. These materials had prompted ED to issue the communication under Section 66(2) of PMLA recommending the registration of an FIR. The court observed that the rejection of a complaint did not prevent the filing of a fresh complaint or the initiation of prosecution if adequate material became available later. It further held that the earlier court orders would not stand in the way of an effective investigation based on the material disclosed in ED’s communication.
Article Summary: Kerala High Court on Friday directed the vigilance director to register an FIR against former chief minister Pinarayi Vijayan, his daughter T Veena and her husband, former minister P A Mohamed Riyas. The case arose from an ED communication to the state police chief under Section 66(2) of the Prevention of Money Laundering Act.

Article Title: 'Wrongfully confined': CJP legal head moves court against police for detention during lawyers' stir
Article Text:
In her plea, Ratna Singh has claimed that her life and liberty are under threat. She has sought legal action against the personnel allegedly involved in restraining her.

Lawyers detained near Supreme Court

CJP legal head seeks judicial intervention

NEW DELHI: Ratna Singh, legal affairs head of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), has moved a Delhi court seeking registration of an FIR against police personnel. She has filed it alleging that police personnel confined her and prevented her from joining a lawyers’ protest against chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over the conduct of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR). In her application filed on Saturday, Singh also sought a status report from the police on the alleged incident.Singh filed the application before chief metropolitan magistrate Abhinav Pandey at Saket district court. She has sought directions for registration of an FIR against the police personnel allegedly involved. She has also asked the court to call for a status report from the concerned authorities.According to the application, Singh is a practising advocate. She was proceeding towards the Supreme Court with two fellow advocates to participate in a protest by lawyers against the CEC and the SIR exercise.The plea alleges that Singh was later sitting in a car with advocate Tara Narula outside her residence when she was prevented from moving. Two cars allegedly blocked her vehicle from the front and rear. Police personnel remained outside the car, preventing her from proceeding further.Singh has alleged that the police personnel did not explain the legal basis for restricting her movement, despite her asking them to do so. She has described the alleged incident as wrongful restraint and confinement.The application also refers to a police call made in connection with the incident and provides details of the call. Singh has raised concerns over her safety and liberty. She has argued that the circumstances warrant urgent intervention by the court.Singh has further stated that a video of the alleged incident may be examined by the court. In her plea, she has claimed that her life and liberty are under threat. She has sought legal action against the personnel allegedly involved in restraining her.The application comes amid protests by members of the legal fraternity against the chief election commissioner and the SIR exercise. The proposed demonstration has brought attention to the right of lawyers to assemble and express their views, as well as the role of police authorities in regulating protests and maintaining law and order.On Saturday, a group of lawyers holding a protest march against the chief election commissioner and the SIR exercise were detained by personnel of the Delhi Police and the Central Reserve Police Force near the Supreme Court.The detentions prompted the Supreme Court Bar Association (SCBA) to urgently approach Chief Justice of India Surya Kant. The association wrote to the CJI about several advocates being detained while peacefully protesting outside the Supreme Court.According to the SCBA's communication, the detained lawyers were taken to Yamuna Sports Complex. The association raised concerns over the detention and sought the CJI's intervention.Following the SCBA's urgent communication, the CJI conveyed to the authorities that the detained lawyers should be released.The detention of the lawyers and Singh's allegations have brought the police action surrounding the protest into focus. While the lawyers were detained near the Supreme Court, Singh has alleged that police personnel separately prevented her from joining the demonstration.Ratna Singh's application seeks judicial intervention over the alleged restriction on her movement. She has asked the court to direct the registration of an FIR against the police personnel allegedly involved in the incident.She has also sought a status report from the concerned authorities to place details of the incident before the court. Her plea refers to the alleged blocking of her vehicle, the presence of police personnel outside it, and the absence of an explanation for the restriction despite her asking for one.Singh has contended that the alleged restraint requires examination by the competent authorities. She has cited concerns over her liberty and personal safety in seeking the court's intervention.The allegations in the application are yet to be established. The plea seeks an FIR and a police status report in connection with the alleged incident.
Article Summary: Ratna Singh, legal affairs head of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), has moved a Delhi court seeking registration of an FIR against police personnel. She has filed it alleging that police personnel confined her and prevented her from joining a lawyers’ protest against chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over the conduct of the Special Intensive Revision.
